requirements.title: Procedure summary argument names are keyword names
requirements.definition: For all procedures defined in the IEEE modules, the displayed argument names are the names used for keyword actual arguments.

pending.procedure-summary-keyword-names: Source-control plan: for each registered Clause 17 procedure, compile a representative conforming call using the argument keywords shown in Tables 17.2 and 17.3 or the detailed procedure description; wrong-keyword mutations are ordinary interface diagnostics owned by generic resolution.

requirements.title: Inquiry functions depend on properties and allow non-value actual arguments
requirements.definition: An inquiry function classified in 17.10 depends on properties of one or more arguments rather than values; unless its own description states otherwise, such arguments may be unallocated allocatables or undefined or disassociated pointers. A transformational function is neither inquiry nor elemental.

pending.inquiry-functions-property-dependent: Source-control plan: use IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE with two default-real variables of the same kind but different values and assert only the scalar logical result form, not a value-dependent distinction.
pending.inquiry-functions-permit-unallocated-or-: Compile-time and run-time plan: declare an unallocated allocatable real and a disassociated real pointer, pass each to IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE, and assert execution reaches a non-default sentinel assignment without referencing the value; procedures whose own descriptions override this rule are excluded.
pending.transformational-function-class-definiti: Source-use plan: classify IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND and IEEE_SUPPORT_ROUNDING as transformational per Table 17.2, and do not use elemental array-shape propagation as an oracle for those procedures.

requirements.title: Class-code letters identify elemental, simple, inquiry, subroutine, and transformational procedures
requirements.definition: The class column code E means elemental function, ES simple elemental subroutine, I inquiry function, SS simple subroutine, and T transformational function.

pending.class-code-e: Source-control plan: for procedures marked E, future fixtures may use scalar and array actuals while value assertions remain owned by each procedure description.
pending.class-code-es: Source-control plan: for procedures marked ES, future fixtures use scalar and array flags for elemental subroutine behavior while side effects remain owned by each procedure description.
pending.class-code-i: Source-control plan: for procedures marked I, future fixtures exercise property-based inquiry calls, including permitted unallocated or disassociated actuals under p2.
pending.class-code-ss: Source-control plan: for procedures marked SS, future fixtures treat the call as a simple subroutine and observe only the side effect stated by its detailed description.
pending.class-code-t: Source-control plan: for procedures marked T, future fixtures avoid elemental shape or inquiry undefined-argument assumptions beyond the detailed description.

accounting.rationale: Inquiry semantics, inquiry argument permission, and transformational definition are split.
Permits unallocated, undefined, or disassociated actuals unless a procedure description overrides it.
Defines transformational function by exclusion from inquiry and elemental.

review_rationale: Source registration for 17.6-17.10, 17.11, 17.11.1 and 17.11.2: halting, floating-point modes and status, exceptional values, IEEE arithmetic, the procedure summary and general rules, and IEEE_CLASS (batch214). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across three rounds; every IEEE effect is a guarded branch plan keyed to its own support inquiry, with exact 60559 results for infinity and subnormal operands. Source accounting only.
